flawed_step: Claim that the depth in the DFS tree equals the shortest-path distance. DFS can reach a vertex along a longer path before trying a shorter one.
counterexample: Triangle graph with vertices s, a, b and edges s-a, a-b, s-b. Neighbour order: s examines a then b; a examines s then b. Trace: DFS(s) discovers a at depth 1. DFS(a) skips s (already visited) and discovers b at depth 2. When DFS returns to s, b is already visited. So b's discovery depth is 2, but dist(s,b)=1 because of the edge s-b.
assessment_summary: False. In a triangle, DFS reaches b through a at depth 2 even though b is adjacent to s (distance 1).
